title: Unboxing Videos for Product Launches | AIVideosUGC
description: Plan unboxing videos for product launches: a teaser before, a full reveal on launch day, and a closer look after. See what to shoot and make your first clip.
h1: How to Use Unboxing Videos for Product Launches
lead: Unboxing videos for product launches work best as a short teaser, a reveal on launch day, and a closer look once people start asking what is in the box. Start from the package photo or a product link, then add a presenter, a script, and a voice.
summary: Plan three short clips around launch day from one package photo, add the date and price yourself, and keep using the reveal after launch week.

paras: What the clip should show, how that compares with filming an open, the three steps, what you can change, how long to make each one, where the date and price go, and how shops use the set.
sections.alt: Hands hold one plain cream ceramic travel mug above its open blank kraft parcel and tissue.

sections.h2: Show the Product, the Open, and a Voice
paras: Put the product in a presenter's hands so a shopper can judge the size, the shape, and the finish without a studio day.
Show the open itself: a hand on the lid, the tissue, and the item coming out. Tease the closed box, reveal it on launch day, and follow with one closer detail.
Give the box a voice. A short spoken line names what is inside. You edit that line before it is locked. The format fits earbuds, candles, skincare sets, and gift boxes.
sections.alt: Hands open a blank kraft parcel to reveal one plain cream ceramic travel mug wrapped in tissue.

sections.h2: Filming an Open vs Starting From a Photo
paras: Cost. A filmed open pays a person, a location, and an edit. Here a 6 second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. Starter is $24.50 for 200 credits a month, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.
Timing. You start when the package photo exists. You do not hold the launch for a booked crew.
How far it stretches. One photo feeds the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. Each shape is its own clip.
Who has to be there. One person on the shop team can run the three clips.
Another version. A new sentence makes another clip when you want a different opening. The credit cost shows before you start, and a failed job returns the credits.

sections.h2: How to Make a Launch Unboxing in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Start from the package photo, or paste the product link. The link path is [URL to video](page:url-to-video). The box in the clip has to be the one people will receive.
Pick an adult presenter from the [actor library](page:ai-actors), or save one look and use it on the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look.
Let a draft script come from the product page, then cut it to one motion and leave the date and the price out of that line. [Product videos](page:product-videos) cover a demo after the open.

sections.h2: What photo should a product launch unboxing video start from?
paras: Use a clear photo of the product in or next to the packaging people will actually receive, shot in daylight with any print facing the camera.

If the box design is still changing, wait until you can photograph the package people will receive. The clip follows that photo and the box you describe, so a stand-in becomes the box shoppers expect. Count what ships. If the kit includes a cable, a pouch, and a card, those are the items that should come out. A product link can fill the first draft, and you still replace any photo that is not the package you will mail.
sections.alt: Hands place one plain cream ceramic travel mug beside its matching blank kraft parcel and folded tissue.

sections.h2: Which AI unboxing video ideas fit launch week?
paras: Plan a teaser, a reveal, and a closer look, each from the same package photo and each with its own sentence. Use one saved presenter on all three.

The teaser shows the closed box and a hand on the lid. The reveal opens the tissue and lifts the product out. The closer look turns one detail, such as a lid, a clasp, or a cable. [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) fits the closer look when you want a demo after the open. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) fits when the still of the closed box should simply start to move.
sections.alt: Hands lift the lid of a blank kraft parcel to begin revealing one plain cream ceramic travel mug.

sections.h2: How do I write the scene for each launch clip?
paras: Name the box, the hands, and the one motion. Leave the date and the price out of that sentence. A drafted script can suggest the line. You cut it down to that one motion.

The teaser can be "Hands rest on the lid of a plain kraft box, soft daylight." The reveal is "Hands lift the lid and raise one cream mug out of the tissue." The closer look names the one detail you want turned toward the camera. Keep each sentence to one motion. Swap the voice if the tone does not fit the shop, and read the captions before you post.
sections.alt: Hands lift one plain cream ceramic mug with no lid from tissue inside a blank kraft parcel.

sections.h2: What You Can Set on the Launch Clip
paras: Start from a photo or a product link. You do not need a separate editor installed to get the first cut.
Change the script, the voice, the frame, and the colors before you export.
A voice reads the line at a natural pace. Swap it if it does not sound like your shop.
Use 9:16 for a short unboxing clip on TikTok, Reels, or Shorts, 1:1 for a feed, and 16:9 for a product page or a regular YouTube video.
Pick a presenter from the actor library, or save one face for the whole launch week.
Edit the drafted script so the spoken line matches the one motion in the clip. You keep the last word on what is said. The same line can be spoken in another language for a second market.

sections.h2: How long should an unboxing video for new products be?
paras: Use 6 seconds for the teaser, 10 to open and show the product, 15 for a slower reveal, and 30 for a multi-item kit.

Those lengths cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits. The cost shows before each job, and a failed job returns the credits. Each shape is a separate clip. Make the length you need for [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) and another length if the product page should hold the longer open.
sections.alt: Hands set one plain cream ceramic travel mug beside its open blank kraft parcel after the reveal.

sections.h2: How do I add the date and price to a short unboxing clip?
paras: Captions can follow the spoken line. You still type the date, the price, and any code yourself so those characters match the store.

Put the date and a few words such as "Coming soon" on the teaser. Put "Available now" and the price on the reveal. Pick music from the library in the editor, or a track you already licensed for ads. Trim the cut there, then send the file to TikTok or Meta, or download it with no watermark. Post the teaser first, switch to the reveal when the product page is live, and save the closer look for the following week. A catalog can also send the same job through the API. Keep the teaser text short so it reads while the clip plays.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Launch Unboxing
paras: A skincare shop has a presenter lift the bottle out of tissue and name the size that ships.
A gadget shop shows the cable, the pouch, and the card coming out in that order.
A candle shop uses the closed box as the teaser and the lid lift as the reveal.
A food shop keeps the voice on the flavor printed on the jar, not on a claim about results.
A jewelry shop uses the closer look to turn the clasp toward the camera.
A shop with two markets keeps the same open and speaks the line in the other language.
A two-person team makes all three clips from one package photo.
A marketplace seller pastes the listing link, then swaps any photo that is not the mailer they use.
A shop that wants two openings writes a second sentence and keeps the same presenter.
A home shop posts the teaser, then swaps in the reveal on the morning the page goes live.
One real package photo, a saved presenter, three sentences for teaser, reveal, and closer look, and your own date and price on top.

Do not show a box or a part the buyer will not receive. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. Download with no watermark, or send the file to TikTok or Meta, after you have checked the open.

faq.q: How do I make an unboxing video for a launch?
faq.a: Photograph the package people will receive, or paste the product link and replace any photo that is not that package. Pick a presenter, edit the script down to one motion, and check the open before you post.

faq.q: Can I start from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. The link can draft the script and pull photos from the page. The box in the finished clip still has to be the one you will mail.

faq.q: What if the video shows something that is not in my box?
faq.a: Do not post that version. Make it again and name the exact contents, such as a bottle, a pump, and a pouch. Shoppers will compare their package with the open they saw.

faq.q: How long should an unboxing clip be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Six is a teaser, ten opens and shows the product, fifteen is a slower reveal, and thirty covers a multi-item kit.

faq.q: What source photo should I use?
faq.a: Use a clear photo of the product or the package, and list every item in the box. Check the opening, the reveal, and the final contents against the real package.

faq.q: How many credits does an unboxing clip use?
faq.a: A 6-second clip uses 24 credits, 10 seconds uses 40, 15 uses 60, and 30 uses 120. A failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: What if my packaging is still changing?
faq.a: Wait until you can photograph the final package. Describe the box people will receive, not a stand-in.

faq.q: Can one package photo make several launch clips?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the photo, keep one saved presenter, and write a separate sentence for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look.

faq.q: Can I change the voice, the music, and the captions?
faq.a: Yes. Swap the voice, pick a library track or one you licensed, and read the captions. Type the date, the price, and any code yourself.

faq.q: Can I send the clip to TikTok or Meta?
faq.a: Yes. After you check the open, send the file to TikTok or Meta, or download it with no watermark.

cta_lead: Turn one package photo into a teaser, a reveal, or a follow-up clip, then check it against the real box.
